subject: Estoicismo

learner_context.prior_exposure: Secondhand summaries and social-media quotes about Stoicism; no primary texts read (Seneca, Epictetus, Marcus Aurelius).

confirmed_competencies: Can explain the core idea of the dichotomy of control in own words and generate a plausible, correctly-scoped daily-life example (a delayed flight).
knowledge_gaps: No direct reading of primary Stoic texts (Seneca, Epictetus, Marcus Aurelius) -- only secondhand summaries and isolated quotes.
No demonstrated familiarity with the four cardinal virtues (wisdom, courage, justice, temperance) or other core Stoic ethical concepts -- question went unanswered.
No established reflective practice (journaling, brief meditation, evening review) -- the answer described a future aspiration to react more calmly, not a past sustained practice.

recommended_starting_depth.entry_point: Start from first principles: introduce Stoicism's historical context and vocabulary, ground the already-understood dichotomy of control in a primary-source excerpt, then build up the cardinal virtues and ethics before introducing a structured reflective-practice habit.
recommended_starting_depth.skip: Do not re-teach the dichotomy of control from scratch; use it as a bridge into primary-source reading and the virtues.

material_caveats: Question 3 (four cardinal virtues / core ethical concepts) received no answer in the single reply; treated as a full gap rather than a partial competency, not as a second question round.

Question 4's answer described a future intention (reacting more calmly to traffic and delays) rather than a past reflective-practice experience, so evidence about prior practice habits is thin; the conservative assumption is no prior sustained practice.
